# 1 Maccabees Chapter 4 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 4 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/1MA_004_page_001.jpg

---

1. And Gorgias took five thousand men and a thousand picked horsemen, and this force moved out by night
2. to fall upon the camp of the Judeans and to strike them suddenly; and the men of the citadel were guides for him.
3. And Judas heard of it and himself went out with his mighty men to strike the king's force at Emmaus,
4. while the force was still dispersed from the camp.
5. And Gorgias came into the camp of Judas in the night and found no one; and he sought them in the hills, for he said, "These are fleeing from us."
6. And at the approach of day Judas appeared in the plain with three thousand men; but they did not have the armor and the swords they wished.
7. And they saw the camp of the nations, strong and fortified, with cavalry all around it; and these were trained warriors.
8. And Judas said to the men with him, "Do not be afraid of their multitude, and do not tremble at their assault.
9. Remember how our fathers were saved at the Red Sea, when Pharaoh pursued them with a force.
10. And now let us cry to Heaven, if he will have mercy on us and remember the covenant of the fathers, and destroy this army before our face today;
11. and all the nations will know that there is one who redeems and saves Israel."
12. And the foreigners lifted up their eyes and saw them coming against them.
13. And they went out of the camp to battle, and those who were with Judas sounded the trumpet.
14. And they engaged, and the nations were struck and fled to the plain.
15. But all the hindmost fell by the sword; and they pursued them as far as Gazara, and to the plains of Idumea and Azotus and Jamnia; and about three thousand men of them fell.
16. And Judas and his army turned back from pursuing them.
17. And he said to the people, "Do not be greedy for the plunder, for there is battle before us.
18. And Gorgias and his force are in the hill country near us; but stand now against our enemies and fight them, and afterward take the plunder boldly."
19. While Judas was still finishing this speech, a detachment appeared, looking out from the hill country.
20. And they saw that their men had been put to flight and that the camp was burning; for the smoke that was seen revealed what was done.
21. And when they perceived these things they were greatly frightened; and when they also saw the army of Judas in the plain ready for battle,
22. they all fled to the land of the Philistines.
23. Then Judas returned to plunder the camp, and they took much gold and silver, and hyacinth and sea purple, and great riches.
24. And they returned home and sang a hymn and blessed Heaven, for he is good, for his mercy endures forever.
25. And Israel had a great salvation on that day.
26. Now the foreigners who had escaped came and told Lysias all the things that had happened.
27. And when he heard, he was perplexed and discouraged, because things had not come about in Israel as he had wished, nor had it turned out as the king had commanded.
28. And in the next year he gathered sixty thousand choice infantry and five thousand cavalry to make war against them.
29. And they came to Idumea and encamped at Beth-zur, and Judas met them with ten thousand men.
30. And he saw that the army was strong, and he prayed and said, "Blessed are you, O Savior of Israel, who broke the assault of the mighty man by the hand of your servant David, and delivered the camp of the aliens into the hands of Jonathan son of Saul and his armor-bearer.
31. Shut up this army in the hand of your people Israel, and let them be ashamed with their forces and their horsemen.
32. Give them fear, melt the boldness of their strength, let them quake at their destruction.
33. Strike them down with the sword of those who love you, and let all who know your name sing your praises."
34. And they joined battle, and about five thousand men of Lysias's army fell, and they fell before them.
35. And when Lysias saw the rout of his men and the boldness of Judas's force and how ready they were either to live or to die nobly, he departed to Antioch and hired soldiers, that he might come again into Judah with yet greater numbers.
36. Then Judas and his brothers said, "Behold, our enemies are crushed; let us go up to cleanse the sanctuary and to dedicate it."
37. And all the army was gathered together and went up to Mount Zion.
38. And they saw the sanctuary desolated, and the altar profaned, and the gates burned, and shrubs growing in the courts as in a forest or as on one of the mountains, and the priests' chambers broken down.
39. And they tore their garments and made great lamentation, and put ashes on their heads,
40. and fell on their faces to the earth, and they sounded the signal trumpets, and cried toward Heaven.
41. Then Judas commanded men to fight against those in the citadel, until he had cleansed the sanctuary.
42. And he chose blameless priests who had delight in the Torah;
43. and they cleansed the sanctuary and removed the stones of the pollution to an unclean place.
44. And they took counsel concerning the altar of burnt offerings that had been profaned, what they should do with it.
45. And a good counsel came to them to tear it down, lest it be a reproach to them, because the nations had defiled it; and they tore it down.
46. And they laid down the stones in the mountain of the temple in a suitable place, until a prophet should come and give answer concerning them.
47. And they took uncut stones according to the Torah, and built a new altar after the manner of the former;
48. and they built the sanctuary, and the interior of the house, and the courts.
49. And they made new holy vessels, and they brought the lampstand and the altar of incense and the table into the temple.
50. And they burned incense on the altar and lit the lamps upon the lampstand, and they gave light in the temple.
51. And they set the bread upon the table and hung up the curtains, and finished all the works which they had undertaken.
52. And they arose early in the morning of the twenty-fifth day of the ninth month, which is the month Chislev, in the one hundred and forty-eighth year,
53. and offered sacrifice according to the Torah upon the new altar of burnt offerings which they had made.
54. At the time and on the day on which the nations had profaned it, it was dedicated with hymns and harps and lutes and cymbals.
55. And all the people fell on their faces and worshiped and blessed Heaven who had prospered them.
56. And they celebrated the dedication of the altar for eight days, and offered burnt offerings with gladness, and offered a sacrifice of salvation and praise.
57. And they decked the front of the temple with golden crowns and small shields, and they rededicated the gates and the priests' chambers, and fitted them with doors.
58. And there was very great gladness among the people, and the reproach of the nations was turned away.
59. And Judas and his brothers and all the congregation of Israel ordained that the days of the dedication of the altar should be observed with gladness and joy at the appointed season, every year for eight days, from the twenty-fifth of Chislev.
60. In that time they fortified Mount Zion with high walls and strong towers round about, lest the nations come and trample them down, as they had done before.
61. And he stationed forces there to guard it, and he fortified Beth-zur to guard it, that the people might have a stronghold against Idumea.
